entries.clue: Perform, covering double-D with one fan (6)

indicatorNotes.covering: a cover goes over and around what it protects, so ACT wraps round the other letters
indicatorNotes.double: to double something is to make two of it, so D appears twice

blocks.note: an operation, not a convention: 'double' repeats the letter D

annotation.surface: A performer with a double-D cup and a single admirer, suggestive in the Private Eye manner.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a bra size; only the last word, 'fan', is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in its loose sense: an enthusiast hooked on a hobby, as in a jazz or crossword devotee.

entries.clue: One on CIA duty hit bottle (8)

indicatorNotes.hit: the letters of CIA DUTY are knocked about into a new order

annotation.surface: An agent on assignment for the CIA strikes someone with a bottle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' looks like the weapon, but it is British slang for nerve or courage, which is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Bottle is British slang for courage or nerve, and audacity is bold nerve.

entries.clue: Party outside one's Conservative Club (5)

indicatorNotes.outside: DO sits outside the other letters

blocks.note: I (one) plus the S of the possessive

annotation.surface: A party held outside a local Conservative Club.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Conservative Club' reads as one institution, but the clue splits there: C ends the wordplay and 'Club' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym by type: a nightclub where people dance to recorded music is a club of this kind.

entries.clue: Vital energy versus drink (7)

blocks.note: chi is the life force in Chinese thought

annotation.surface: A health slogan pitting vital energy against alcohol.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sets energy against drink as rivals, but the two words simply stand side by side.
annotation.definitionFit: Chianti is an Italian red wine, so a drink.

entries.clue: International body moved fast, prepared to expose member? (8)

annotation.surface: The UN acting quickly, ready to name and shame one of its member states.
annotation.walkthrough: The member sounds like a UN member state; the question mark flags the rude reading of trousers opened.
annotation.definitionFit: Having undone your flies, you are unzipped and ready to expose your member.

entries.clue: Low point is Newcastle etc getting ditched by Dorries, right? (5)

indicatorNotes.getting ditched by: NE is dropped from the name

blocks.note: Nadine Dorries, the former Conservative culture secretary
Newcastle and its neighbours make up England's North East; its initials NE are the letters removed

annotation.surface: Nadine Dorries turning her back on Newcastle, a low point for the Tory right.
annotation.walkthrough: Dorries must be turned into her first name, NADINE; NE is the North East, the region Newcastle belongs to.
annotation.definitionFit: An astronomy term, the point of the sky directly underfoot, borrowed for the worst moment of any career or fortune.

entries.clue: Innocent of having accepted dope, you exhale finally (7)

indicatorNotes.finally: take the last letter of exhale

blocks.note: dope and gen both mean information

annotation.surface: Pleading innocent to taking drugs because you never inhaled, a nod to Bill Clinton's defence.
annotation.walkthrough: Dope looks like drugs but means information here, as gen does.
annotation.definitionFit: An ingenue is an innocent, unworldly young woman.

entries.clue: Unseemly being in this shit – right awful state (4,5)

annotation.definitionNote: The adjective matches the phrase 'in poor taste'; 'being in' carries the IN.

indicatorNotes.awful: something awful is in a bad way, so the letters of STATE are in a bad order

annotation.surface: A despairing cry that the country is in a right awful mess.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Right' reads as an intensifier (a right mess) but supplies R; the clue is itself in poor taste, which is the point.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a remark that is improper or indecent is said to be in poor taste.

entries.clue: Choice of improvised duel with former lover on the rebound (2,4)

indicatorNotes.improvised: something improvised is made up on the spot, so DUEL is put together in a new order
indicatorNotes.on the rebound: a ball on the rebound comes back the way it went, so EX is read backwards

blocks.note: an ex; turned round to XE

annotation.surface: Picking a fight with a new partner out of spite, while on the rebound from an ex.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the rebound' sounds like romance after a break-up but tells you to reverse EX.
annotation.definitionFit: Choice as an adjective means of top quality, which is de luxe.

entries.clue: Exited, clutching small girl – let go! (9)

blocks.note: to exit is to die, as in exit this life

annotation.surface: Someone walks out holding a little girl while another shouts at them to let her go.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Let go!' reads as a shouted order, but it is the definition, in its sense of sacked.
annotation.definitionFit: A euphemism: employers say they 'let go' staff when they sack them.

entries.clue: Celebrity arses about with Raab in familiar fashion? (7)

indicatorNotes.about: to turn about is to face the other way, so RATS is read backwards
indicatorNotes.in familiar fashion: Raab by a pet form of his first name, Dominic

blocks.note: arses and rats are both contemptible people; turned about to STAR
Dominic Raab, the former Tory minister, shortened

annotation.surface: A famous person larking about with Dominic Raab on first-name terms.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Arses about' reads as messing around, but 'about' belongs to the rats; Raab's first name is Dominic, so DOM.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym for the condition of being famous, not for the famous person the word also names.

entries.clue: Pull back having imbibed house spirit (5)

indicatorNotes.back: LUG is turned round to GUL
indicatorNotes.having imbibed: to imbibe is to drink in, so GUL swallows HO and holds it inside

blocks.note: to lug is to pull; reversed to GUL

annotation.surface: Someone pulls back after downing a house spirit at the bar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'House spirit' sounds like the pub's own-label spirit; 'spirit' alone is the definition, a ghostly one.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: in Arabic folklore the ghoul is a grave-robbing demon, one kind of evil spirit.

entries.clue: Start to come down on Braverman, finally – buffoon! (5)

indicatorNotes.Start to: take the first letter of come
indicatorNotes.finally: take the last letter of Braverman

annotation.surface: A call to start cracking down on Suella Braverman, the former Home Secretary, dismissed as a buffoon.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Come down on' reads as a phrasal verb, but it breaks into C, LOW and a join.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both name a fool who makes others laugh, or a person not to be taken seriously.

entries.clue: Expert in a new type of personal protection (5)

indicatorNotes.in: in means placed within, so the expert is put inside the other letters

annotation.surface: A specialist in a new kind of personal protection equipment.
annotation.walkthrough: Personal protection suggests bodyguards or PPE; an apron protects your clothes.
annotation.definitionFit: An apron is worn to protect the wearer's clothes.

entries.clue: (& 25ac.) Vote-seeking measure? Try getting chop! (3)

blocks.note: to tax is to try or strain, as in taxing your patience

annotation.surface: A cynical view of election bribes, with an exasperated cry to try axing something.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs on into 25 across. 'Try' sounds like making an attempt; it means strain, which is to tax.
annotation.definitionFit: Governments cut taxes to win votes, so a tax cut is a vote-seeking measure.

entries.clue: (& 18ac.) Those people at possibly deadliest world trouble spot (3,6)

indicatorNotes.possibly: DEADLIEST is one possible arrangement of the letters

annotation.surface: Pointing at the people in what may be the deadliest trouble spot on earth.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs on into 18 across. The grim surface happens to be literally true of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: The Middle East is a region notorious for conflict.

entries.clue: Say entire fiasco is an early sign of a regular tosser? (9)

annotation.definition: an early sign of a regular tosser?
annotation.surface: A mock-medical warning about the tell-tale signs of a habitual idiot.
annotation.walkthrough: Tosser is British slang for an idiot and also for a masturbator; the old myth says self-abuse makes you go blind, and eyestrain comes first.
annotation.definitionFit: Playground folklore held that frequent masturbation damaged the eyes, so eyestrain would be its early symptom.

entries.clue: Made certain condemned leader goes (7)

blocks.note: condemned = censured; first letter C removed

annotation.surface: A condemned party leader is ousted, and someone made sure of it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leader' suggests a political leader, but it is only the first letter of CENSURED.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the past tense: someone who made sure of an outcome guaranteed it.

entries.clue: see 15ac. (4)
Rubbished NHS on cue, so not elected (8)

indicatorNotes.Rubbished: the letters of NHS ON CUE are trashed and rearranged

annotation.surface: A party trashed the NHS right on cue, and so lost the election.
annotation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service, a subject no party can be seen to attack.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a candidate the voters passed over was not chosen by them.

entries.clue: (& 28ac.) The latest intrusion experienced by listeners? (4)

blocks.note: a bulletin that interrupts a radio programme

annotation.surface: A complaint about the newest interruption suffered by radio audiences.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs on into 28 across. The question mark hints at a cheekier reading: an exposure a flasher inflicts, here on people who can only hear it.
annotation.definitionFit: A news flash brings the latest news and breaks into the programme listeners were hearing.

entries.clue: Rock star and neo-politician (7)

indicatorNotes.Rock: STAR and NEO are shaken together

annotation.surface: A rock star who is also a newcomer to politics.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rock star' is a ready-made phrase, but 'Rock' is the anagram instruction and the hyphen detaches 'neo' from 'politician'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: senators sit in upper houses such as the US Senate, so they are politicians.

entries.clue: What a bad administration would do with minister almost overwhelmed by miners' action (9)

annotation.definition: What a bad administration would do

indicatorNotes.overwhelmed by: GOV is swamped by the other letters
indicatorNotes.action: MINERS are set in motion into a new order

blocks.note: Michael Gove, a long-serving Tory minister, without his last letter

annotation.surface: A cabinet minister nearly swept away by industrial action by miners.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Minister' must be a particular one, Gove; 'miners' action' sounds like a strike but tells you to rearrange MINERS.
annotation.definitionFit: A bad administration governs badly, which is to misgovern.

entries.clue: Seedy party's illegal position (7)

blocks.note: feeling seedy is feeling off, unwell
a side in a dispute is a party

annotation.surface: A sleazy political party caught holding an unlawful stance.
annotation.walkthrough: The political reading hides a sports one: offside is the illegal position in football.
annotation.definitionFit: Offside is an illegal position for a player in football and other games.

entries.clue: Cry "Quit protecting aide's back!" (6)

indicatorNotes.back: take the last letter of aide's

annotation.surface: A shouted order to stop covering for an assistant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cry' introduces the quotation in the surface, but it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a scream is a loud, high cry of fear or pain.

entries.clue: see 14ac. (3)
New woman joining right? I'm amazed! (5)

annotation.surface: Astonishment at news that a new female member is joining the right.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Never!' is the exclamation of disbelief, just as 'I'm amazed!' is.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Never!' is an exclamation of surprise, equivalent to 'I'm amazed!'.

entries.clue: Bring up Vennell's inception? Leave it out! (5)

indicatorNotes.inception: the start of the name, its first letter

annotation.surface: Raising Paula Vennells, the Post Office boss of the Horizon scandal, meets a cry of 'give over!'.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leave it out!' is London slang for 'stop it'; here it is OMIT.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal-verb synonym: 'bring up' means throw up your stomach contents, not raise a topic.

entries.clue: see 20ac. (5)
Watchful royal consort releases book (5)

indicatorNotes.releases: to release is to set free, so the name lets go of one of its letters

annotation.surface: An attentive royal spouse brings out a book.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Releases book' sounds like publishing, but it means dropping a B.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone alert is on the lookout, keeping watch.

entries.clue: Nice to get money by force? (5)

blocks.note: nice in its old sense of precise
to demand payment with threats, the verb sense

annotation.surface: A wry remark that it is pleasant to squeeze money out of people.
annotation.walkthrough: Nice here is not pleasant but fine and precise, as in a nice distinction.
annotation.definitionFit: Nice can mean precise, and to exact money is to demand it with force.

entries.clue: Undid pants – in trouble for lack of clarity (9)

indicatorNotes.pants: British slang for rubbish, so UNDID is garbled

annotation.surface: Someone who dropped their trousers and landed in trouble over some confusion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like underwear being undone, but it is British slang for rubbish, telling you to jumble UNDID.
annotation.definitionFit: Muddy water is cloudy, and the word extends to muddled thinking or prose that is hard to follow.

entries.clue: Car circles round right heartless Tory? That's not the half of it (8)

annotation.definition: That's not the half of it

indicatorNotes.circles: MINI goes round the other letters

annotation.surface: A car circling a rightwing Tory without a heart, with a hint that there is more to the story.
annotation.walkthrough: 'That's not the half of it' is a cute definition: a minority is less than half the whole.
annotation.definitionFit: A minority is a group smaller than half, so not the half of it.

entries.clue: Church official, gender not resolved (6)

indicatorNotes.resolved: NOT is sorted into a new order

annotation.surface: A church officer whose gender remains undecided, a dig at church rows over gender.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not resolved' reads as undecided, but 'resolved' is the instruction to rearrange NOT.
annotation.definitionFit: A sexton is a church officer who looks after the building and churchyard.
